.AES
[cols="2h,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Algorithm |AES-GCM |AES block cipher

|Names
|`gcm`, `aes128_gcm`, `aes256_gcm`
|`aes128`, `aes192`, `aes256`

|AEAD
|yes
|no

|Key
|16, 24 or 32 bytes
|16, 24 or 32 bytes

|Nonce (IV)
|1 to 128 bytes; 12 recommended
|none

|Nonce misuse
|not resistant: a repeated IV under one key reveals the plaintexts' XOR and lets tags be forged (link:https://csrc.nist.gov/csrc/media/projects/block-cipher-techniques/documents/bcm/comments/800-38-series-drafts/gcm/joux_comments.pdf[A. Joux, Authentication Failures in NIST version of GCM, 2006], link:https://eprint.iacr.org/2016/475[H. Boeck et al., Nonce-Disrespecting Adversaries, 2016])
|none: a block cipher takes no nonce, and equal blocks give equal ciphertext

|Speed, with and without hardware support
|seal of 16 KiB, 256-bit key: native, BearSSL 115 µs, OpenSSL 2.6 µs; wasip2, BearSSL 134 µs, OpenSSL 129 µs; wasip3, BearSSL 130 µs, OpenSSL 122 µs; emscripten, BearSSL 150 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)
|encryption of one 16-byte block, 256-bit key: native, OpenSSL 0.0624 µs, ctaes 0.473 µs; wasip2, OpenSSL 0.0991 µs, ctaes 0.504 µs; wasip3, OpenSSL 0.0961 µs, ctaes 0.451 µs; emscripten, ctaes 0.45 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)

|Constant time, by design
|BearSSL and OpenSSL with assembly: yes (link:https://www.bearssl.org/constanttime.html[BearSSL, constant-time crypto]; link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/aes/asm[OpenSSL's AES assembly for ARMv8 and x86-64]); OpenSSL no-asm (MSVC, wasip2, wasip3): no (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/INSTALL.md[OpenSSL's INSTALL.md, no-asm])
|ctaes: yes (link:https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/tree/master/src/crypto/ctaes[ctaes, constant-time AES]); OpenSSL with assembly: yes (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/tree/master/crypto/aes/asm[OpenSSL's AES assembly for ARMv8 and x86-64]); OpenSSL no-asm: no (link:https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/master/crypto/aes/aes_core.c[OpenSSL's crypto/aes/aes_core.c, OPENSSL_AES_CONST_TIME])

|Constant time, measured
|BearSSL: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten. OpenSSL (seal alone: its open branches on the verdict inside OpenSSL): native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3 (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|OpenSSL: not measured yet. ctaes: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)

|Standards
|link:https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/38/d/final[NIST SP 800-38D, GCM and GMAC]
|link:https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/197/final[FIPS 197, the Advanced Encryption Standard]

|Where it is used
|TLS 1.3 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-9.1[RFC 8446, TLS 1.3, section 9.1]), SSH (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5647[RFC 5647, AES-GCM for SSH]), IPsec (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4106[RFC 4106, GCM in IPsec ESP]), SRTP (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7714[RFC 7714, AES-GCM for SRTP]), optional for WebRTC's media (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8827[RFC 8827, WebRTC security architecture])
|none on its own: every AES mode is built on it

|Browsers' WebCrypto
|yes, with 16- or 32-byte keys (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API]; link:https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/components/webcrypto/status.cc[Chromium's WebCrypto refuses 192-bit AES keys])
|no raw block cipher (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])

|Choose it when
|a protocol, a browser's WebCrypto or a standard names AES-GCM, or the CPU has AES instructions; at most 2^32 messages per key with random IVs, otherwise a counter
|you need one keyed permutation of a 16-byte block, such as an opaque identifier; for data, use an AEAD
|===

.ChaCha20-Poly1305
[cols="2h,5,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Algorithm |ChaCha20-Poly1305 |ChaCha20-Poly1305, original |XChaCha20-Poly1305

|Names
|`chacha20_poly1305`
|`chacha20_poly1305_original`
|`xchacha20_poly1305`

|AEAD
|yes
|yes
|yes

|Key
|32 bytes
|32 bytes
|32 bytes

|Nonce (IV)
|12 bytes
|8 bytes, too short to draw at random: a counter
|24 bytes, safe to draw at random for every message

|Nonce misuse
|not resistant: a repeated nonce under one key reveals the plaintexts' XOR and lets tags be forged (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8439#section-4[RFC 8439, section 4: a nonce is never repeated under one key])
|not resistant (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305[libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions])
|not resistant to a repeated nonce, but 24 random bytes never repeat in practice (link:https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha[draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha, XChaCha20-Poly1305])

|Speed, with and without hardware support
|seal of 16 KiB, 256-bit key: native, BearSSL 27.2 µs, OpenSSL 9.04 µs, libsodium 26.7 µs; wasip2, BearSSL 64.9 µs, OpenSSL 45.8 µs, libsodium 34.6 µs; wasip3, BearSSL 70.5 µs, OpenSSL 46.3 µs, libsodium 35.1 µs; emscripten, BearSSL 52.5 µs, libsodium 30.3 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)
|seal of 16 KiB, 256-bit key: native, libsodium 25.7 µs; wasip2, libsodium 34.5 µs; wasip3, libsodium 52.5 µs; emscripten, libsodium 30.5 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)
|seal of 16 KiB, 256-bit key: native, libsodium 26.7 µs; wasip2, libsodium 36.3 µs; wasip3, libsodium 41.5 µs; emscripten, libsodium 30 µs (2026-11-21, Apple M5 Max, under load: read the spread, provisional; <<crypto-performance>>)

|Constant time, by design
|libsodium, BearSSL and OpenSSL: yes, additions, XORs and rotations with no table indexed by a secret (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8439#section-2.1[RFC 8439, section 2.1: ChaCha's quarter round, additions, XORs and rotations of 32-bit words]; link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead[libsodium's documentation, AEAD constructions: ChaCha20 and timing attacks])
|libsodium: yes (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead[libsodium's documentation, AEAD constructions: ChaCha20 and timing attacks])
|libsodium: yes (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead[libsodium's documentation, AEAD constructions: ChaCha20 and timing attacks])

|Constant time, measured
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten. BearSSL: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang) and dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; wasip2, dudect (judged off the runners GitHub hosts), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip3, emscripten. OpenSSL (seal alone: its open branches on the verdict inside OpenSSL): native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3 (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)

|Standards
|link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8439[RFC 8439, ChaCha20 and Poly1305 for IETF Protocols]
|none: libsodium's original construction (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305[libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions])
|link:https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha[draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha, XChaCha20-Poly1305]

|Where it is used
|TLS 1.3 (link:https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8446#section-9.1[RFC 8446, TLS 1.3, section 9.1]), WireGuard (link:https://www.wireguard.com/protocol/[WireGuard's protocol, cryptography])
|none in new protocols: the format of libsodium's `crypto_aead_chacha20poly1305` (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead/chacha20-poly1305[libsodium's ChaCha20-Poly1305 constructions])
|libsodium's secretstream (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretstream[libsodium's documentation, encrypted streams (secretstream, on XChaCha20-Poly1305)])

|Browsers' WebCrypto
|no: WebCrypto offers AES-GCM, not ChaCha20-Poly1305 (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|no (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|no (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])

|Choose it when
|a protocol names RFC 8439's AEAD (TLS 1.3, WireGuard), or the program runs without AES hardware and numbers its nonces with a counter; to draw nonces at random, XChaCha20-Poly1305
|the peer writes libsodium's original construction; otherwise RFC 8439's form or XChaCha20-Poly1305
|you encrypt many messages under one key and want to draw each nonce at random: a chat app, records in a database, on the web and natively alike; when in doubt, this one
|===

.Secret boxes
[cols="2h,5,5",options="header"]
|===
|Algorithm |XSalsa20-Poly1305 (NaCl's secret box) |XChaCha20-Poly1305 secret box

|Names
|`secretbox`
|`secretbox_xchacha20poly1305`

|AEAD
|yes, without additional data
|yes, without additional data

|Key
|32 bytes
|32 bytes

|Nonce (IV)
|24 bytes, safe to draw at random
|24 bytes, safe to draw at random

|Nonce misuse
|not resistant to a repeated nonce; random ones never repeat in practice (link:https://cr.yp.to/snuffle/xsalsa-20081128.pdf[D. J. Bernstein, Extending the Salsa20 nonce, 2008])
|not resistant to a repeated nonce; random ones never repeat in practice (link:https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha[draft-irtf-cfrg-xchacha, XChaCha20-Poly1305])

|Speed, with and without hardware support
|not measured yet
|not measured yet

|Constant time, by design
|libsodium: yes, additions, XORs and rotations with no table lookup (link:https://cr.yp.to/snuffle/design.pdf[D. J. Bernstein, Salsa20 design: why add-rotate-xor])
|libsodium: yes (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/aead[libsodium's documentation, AEAD constructions: ChaCha20 and timing attacks])

|Constant time, measured
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)
|libsodium: native, Valgrind's memcheck (Linux) and MemorySanitizer (Linux, clang), nothing found; not measured yet on wasip2, wasip3, emscripten (<<crypto-backends-constant-time>>)

|Standards
|none: NaCl's construction (link:https://nacl.cr.yp.to/secretbox.html[NaCl, secret-key authenticated encryption (crypto_secretbox)])
|none: libsodium's construction (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox[libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption])

|Where it is used
|programs that read or write NaCl's and libsodium's `crypto_secretbox` (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox[libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption])
|programs on libsodium's `crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305` (link:https://doc.libsodium.org/secret-key_cryptography/secretbox[libsodium's documentation, secret-key authenticated encryption])

|Browsers' WebCrypto
|no (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])
|no (link:https://www.w3.org/TR/WebCryptoAPI/[W3C Web Cryptography API])

|Choose it when
|the data must be read by a program on NaCl's or libsodium's `crypto_secretbox`; otherwise XChaCha20-Poly1305, which also authenticates additional data
|the peer writes libsodium's `crypto_secretbox_xchacha20poly1305`; otherwise `xchacha20_poly1305`
|===
